channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: The trouble with Belgium: In Brussels, 'good enough' is good enough
item.description: Work here is not character-defining but adjacent to one’s identity: we can do things quickly, and then enjoy life. Or even the other way around.

item.title: Brussels Flemish community further develops BRUZZKet news platform for children
item.description: The platform produces child-friendly news and encourages young people in Brussels to try journalism for themselves.

item.title: The Brussels Times Gig Guide: What are the best concerts this November?
item.description: Check out this month's unmissable gigs in the Belgian capital for your and your friends to enjoy.

item.title: ‘Every day, we send people back onto the street’: Brussels struggles with rising crack addiction
item.description: “There has been no inflation on cocaine for many years. That gram you paid €50 for ten years ago still costs €50.”

item.title: Five-day Golden Afro Artistic Awards launches in Brussels
item.description: There will be exhibitions and concerts at various venues across the capital, including Bozar and the La Médiatine art gallery.

item.title: Six sentenced following attempted abduction with an AR-15 rifle in Brussels
item.description: One of the six defendants is currently serving in the army and asked the court to suspend the ruling or impose a community service sentence, but the court rejected the request.

item.title: Brussels is bilingual - What about its hospitals?
item.description: In Brussels, the rules are strict: if you are treated in a hospital emergency department, you must be able to receive assistance in Dutch and French.

item.title: Dear Kristina: 'I wish I could bring my dog to the office'
item.description: "My job involves long days, late meetings and networking events. I live alone with my dog, and I feel guilty about how much time she spends by herself."

item.title: Brussels unemployment benefit claims fall 50% in a year
item.description: Belgium as a whole saw a 38% drop in unemployment benefits claims in a year, after a new limit capping them at two years for the first time was introduced.

item.title: All Saints' Weekend: longer cemetery hours and diverted buses in Brussels
item.description: STIB-MIVB will extend some bus routes to make cemeteries easier to reach, as private transport is often banned at cemeteries.

item.title: Brussels Prosecutor's Office spokesperson charged with leaking confidential i-Police documents
item.description: Belgian opposition parties are demanding transparency and a parliamentary inquiry after two spokespersons were charged in connection with the failed i-Police project.

item.title: Brussels' Kanal Museum site reopened following reports of gas leak
item.description: Firefighters, police and gas network operator Sibelga were sent to the scene to trace the source of the potential gas leak, according to the Brussels fire service.

item.title: New Belgian intersex association calls for end to non-consensual medical interventions
item.description: A new organisation is calling for an end to intersex variations being treated as a medical or psychiatric disorder in Belgium.

item.title: Brussels police defend seizing 'illegal' swimming goggles at protest
item.description: Among the nabbed items were goggles, eye serum and medical face masks. Police later admitted that these objects are not, by themselves, illegal.

item.title: New storm prompts over 60 crisis calls in Brussels
item.description: Storm Boelo caused severe damage in Brussels on Saturday, with most people getting help with flooding and fallen trees.

item.title: Lost for 75 years, Horta’s Art Nouveau masterpiece is returning to the public
item.description: More than seven decades after its demolition, one of Victor Horta’s most remarkable creations is being brought back into the spotlight.

item.title: Greens call for clarity over tree felling in Brussels
item.description: One person was seriously injured when a tree fell on a terrace, but the backlash now centres on whether cutting down all the square’s trees set a troubling precedent.

item.title: Police arrest nine protesters after Brussels demonstrations
item.description: After deploying water cannons and pepper spray, police also arrested nine people during the Brussels demonstrations, only five of whom were actively protesting.

item.title: Brussels spectacle stood for months without valid permit
item.description: The ticketed spectacle stood for over two and a half months without a planning permit. The environmental permit might have been missing, too.

item.title: Brussels parks and Sonian Forest closed due to Storm Austen
item.description: All parks, nature reserves and forests are expected to reopen on Monday as Storm Austen continues to ravage Western Europe.
